facts: New York City served as the first capital of the United States under the Constitution from 1789 to 1790.
Central Park was designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and Calvert Vaux and opened in 1858.
The New York City Marathon is the largest marathon in the world, featuring thousands of runners annually across five boroughs.
More than 800 languages are spoken in New York City, making it the most linguistically diverse city on Earth.
The iconic Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States in 1886.
Central Park's main running loop stretches six miles, offering a famous scenic route for local distance runners.
Dutch settlers originally established the city in 1624 as a trading post named New Amsterdam.
The Brooklyn Bridge opened in 1883 and was the world's longest suspension bridge at that time.
Wall Street in Lower Manhattan is famous globally as the historic financial heart of the United States.
Pizza arrived in America when the first U.S. pizzeria opened in Manhattan's Little Italy in 1905.
The Empire State Building was completed in 1931 and stood as the world's tallest building for forty years.
Times Square earned its famous nickname after the New York Times moved its headquarters there in 1904.
New York City consists of five distinct boroughs: Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Staten Island.
The High Line is an elevated linear park built on a former historic freight rail line on Manhattan's West Side.
Broadway is famous worldwide as the center of American commercial theater and live performance arts.
Staten Island Ferry offers free scenic rides with breathtaking views of New York Harbor and the skyline.
The iconic bagels of New York owe their legendary texture to the city's soft municipal water supply.
Grete Waitz won the New York City Marathon a record nine times between 1978 and 1988.
Van Cortlandt Park in the Bronx features one of the oldest and most famous cross-country running courses in America.
Flushing Meadows Corona Park in Queens hosted two World's Fairs and now hosts the US Open tennis tournament.
